title: Dependency-Aware Circuit Scheduling for Multi-Core Quantum Systems to Minimize Makespan
authors: Rajeswari Suance P S, Ruchika Gupta, Maurizio Palesi, John Jose
abstract: Multi-core quantum computing architectures have emerged as a promising solution to the qubit scalability limitations of monolithic NISQ devices. Quantum algorithms are expressed as quantum circuits composed of single- and two-qubit gates. However, circuit scheduling in multi-core quantum systems remains largely unexplored. Reducing overall execution time (makespan), increasing core utilization, and hiding communication latency behind computation depends on effective scheduling. In this paper, we first introduce a layered scheduling approach as a baseline where quantum gates within the same layer are executed in parallel, while layers themselves are executed sequentially. We then propose a greedy scheduling strategy which schedules each gate as soon as all its dependencies and required resources are available. This allows fine-grained parallelism across cores. Our evaluation shows that on real benchmarks, greedy scheduling achieves an average 40% reduction in makespan and improvement in core utilization. The results suggest that the use of intelligent circuit scheduling to exploit parallelism can greatly enhance the speed of circuit execution in multi-core quantum architectures.
summary: This paper addresses the critical challenge of efficiently scheduling quantum circuits across multiple interconnected quantum cores. By proposing a dependency-aware greedy algorithm over a simple layer-by-layer approach, the authors demonstrate significant speedups by exploiting fine-grained parallelism and better managing communication latency. This work provides crucial insights for optimizing future multi-core quantum hardware implementations.
main_problem: The primary goal is to minimize the overall execution time (makespan) when running quantum circuits on multi-core quantum computing architectures.
main_result: A dependency-aware greedy scheduling strategy was shown to achieve an average 40% reduction in makespan and improve core utilization compared to baseline layered scheduling on real benchmarks.
method: The authors compare a simple, sequential 'layered scheduling' approach against a proposed fine-grained, dependency-aware greedy heuristic that schedules gates as soon as all prerequisites and resources are available.
model_or_system: The model is a multi-core quantum system structured on an n x n 2D mesh topology. Inter-core operations require quantum teleportation due to the no-cloning theorem, introducing significant communication latency.
key_observables: Makespan (T_total), Core Utilization, and Communication Overlap Ratio (R_comm).
important_parameters: The system size is defined by the mesh topology ($n 	imes n$) and the number of qubits per core ($Q_i$). Inter-core communication delay ($	ext{com time}$) is a critical parameter.
main_assumptions: Assumes deterministic teleportation with successful entanglement generation, and that inter-core communication latency is orders of magnitude higher than local gate execution latency.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the multi-core architecture (NoC), compare makespans between layered vs. greedy scheduling on case studies, and show performance metrics across varying mesh sizes using synthetic and real benchmarks.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the physical model of a multi-core quantum processor. It then introduces two scheduling methods: baseline layered scheduling and the proposed dependency-aware greedy heuristic. The core of the work involves rigorous evaluation against various benchmarks to quantify performance gains.
why_interesting: While focused on classical scheduling algorithms, the explicit modeling of resource constraints (qubit availability, entanglement links) and communication overhead is highly relevant for understanding practical limitations in building large-scale quantum simulators or hardware control stacks.

Fig. 4a shows the comparative study of makespan for syn- thetic random circuits across different hardware configurations. We can see that proposed greedy scheduling algorithm con- sistently achieves a lower makespan than layered scheduling. This improvement arises because the greedy approach exploits inter-layer parallelism, allowing gates to execute as soon as their dependencies and resources are available. In contrast, the layered scheduling ignores the fine-grained parallelism and fails to hide inter-core communication latency, which is particularly evident for the larger meshes.
